name: Python Handbook
articles: Variables and types
A variable is made by giving it a value. Python works out the type by itself: whole numbers, decimals, text, or true and false.
variable variables type types int float str string bool number assign

name = "Ada"        # text (str)
age = 36            # whole number (int)
height = 1.68       # decimal (float)
is_admin = True     # bool

print(type(age))    # <class 'int'>
py
Print and input
print shows something; input waits for the user to type and always gives back text.
print input output read ask user type console show

name = input("What is your name? ")
age = int(input("How old are you? "))     # turn the text into a number

print(f"Hello {name}, next year you will be {age + 1}.")
py
If, elif and else
The condition ends with a colon, and the lines that belong to it are indented by four spaces.
if elif else condition conditional compare check
py
Loops
"for" goes through the items of something; range gives numbers to count with. "while" repeats as long as its condition holds.
loop loops for while range repeat iterate count each

for i in range(1, 4):          # 1, 2, 3
    print(i)

for fruit in ["apple", "pear"]:
    print(fruit)

n = 3
while n > 0:
    print(n)
    n -= 1
py
Functions
A function is defined with "def". It can have default values, and gives its result back with "return".
function functions def return parameters arguments define call default

def greet(name, greeting="Hello"):
    return f"{greeting}, {name}!"

print(greet("Ada"))                 # Hello, Ada!
print(greet("Alan", "Good day"))    # Good day, Alan!
py
Lists
A list is an ordered collection that can change. Items are counted from zero, and a slice takes a part of it.
list lists array append remove index slice sort len items

nums = [3, 8, 12]
nums.append(20)             # [3, 8, 12, 20]
print(nums[0], nums[-1])    # 3 20
print(nums[1:3])            # [8, 12]
print(len(nums), sorted(nums, reverse=True))
py
List comprehensions
A comprehension builds a new list from another in one line, optionally keeping only some of the items.
list comprehension map filter one line new list squares

nums = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
squares = [n * n for n in nums]              # [1, 4, 9, 16, 25]
evens = [n for n in nums if n % 2 == 0]      # [2, 4]
py
Dictionaries
A dictionary pairs keys with values. Use .get to read a key that may not be there.
dictionary dict key value pairs map lookup get items
py
Work with text
Strings have methods to change case, split, join and replace. An f-string puts values straight into text.
string strings text upper lower split join replace format fstring length

name = "Ada Lovelace"
print(name.upper())              # ADA LOVELACE
print(name.split())              # ['Ada', 'Lovelace']
print("-".join(["a", "b"]))      # a-b
print(name.replace("Ada", "A.")) # A. Lovelace
print(f"{len(name)} characters")
py
Read and write files
Open a file inside "with", so that it is closed for you. "w" writes over the file, "a" adds to its end.
file files read write open save text with lines

with open("notes.txt", "w") as f:
    f.write("First line\n")

with open("notes.txt") as f:
    for line in f:
        print(line.strip())
py
Handle errors
Code that may fail goes under "try". "except" names the error it is ready for.
error errors try except exception raise handle fail valueerror
py
Classes
A class describes a kind of thing: __init__ sets up a new one, and its methods are what it can do.
class classes object objects init self method oop instance
py
Random numbers
The random module gives whole numbers, picks from a list, and shuffles.
random number randint choice shuffle dice pick

import random

print(random.randint(1, 6))                 # 1 to 6
print(random.choice(["red", "green"]))

cards = [1, 2, 3, 4]
random.shuffle(cards)
py
Import modules
A module is a file of ready-made code. Import the whole module, or only the names you need.
import module modules library package from math use

import math
from datetime import date

print(math.sqrt(16))      # 4.0
print(date.today())

Read JSON
The json module turns JSON text into dictionaries and lists, and back again.
json parse load dump data file api dictionary

import json

text = '{"name": "Ada", "langs": ["en", "fr"]}'
data = json.loads(text)
print(data["langs"][0])            # en

print(json.dumps(data, indent=2))
py
Wait and time things
time.sleep pauses the program; time.time gives the seconds since 1970, which is enough to measure how long something took.
time sleep wait delay pause timer measure seconds

import time

start = time.time()
time.sleep(1.5)                         # wait a second and a half
print(f"That took {time.time() - start:.1f} seconds")
